fields.description:
## Problem

`rebar/host:review_interrupts` is published DIMENSIONLESS, but `autodeploy.sh` emits its
`AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT` marker for two causes with a `reason` field that the metric
throws away:

- `bound-exceeded`   — `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` was spent with reviews still in flight. The bot is
                       busy; the drain check is WORKING.
- `signal-unavailable` — `/health`'s `in_flight` was unreadable, so the deploy ran WITHOUT a
                       drain check. The probe itself is broken and every deploy is blind.

These have OPPOSITE remediations, and the alarm cannot tell them apart.

## Why this is worth its own ticket

This is the concrete cost, not a hypothetical. [rebar:7b4a-0f39-1a45-4ce9] was filed by an
automated CloudWatch sweep that could see the firings but not their reason, so it had to hedge
between "the bot is busy" and "34cd has silently regressed and every deploy is blind" — and its
own AC1 was "read the reason from `journalctl` on the box". Answering it required SSM shell
access to i-00880b2c7f13527c5. It turned out to be `bound-exceeded` on all four firings, but
that could not be known from the metric.

The alarm description in `monitoring_autodeploy.tf` already tells the investigator to go read
the journal for the reason field. Splitting the metric removes that hop, and matters most for
`signal-unavailable`, which is the urgent one and is currently indistinguishable from routine
burst residue.

## Scope — observability only, but it needs an apply

Behaviour-preserving for autodeploy and for reviews: nothing about deferral, the bound, or
review execution changes. It is confined to how the existing marker is counted and alarmed.
`autodeploy.sh` is NOT edited: it already stamps the reason.

## Implementation plan

**Chosen shape: distinct journal patterns counted into separate DIMENSIONLESS metrics**, not a
CloudWatch dimension. This mirrors how `observability.sh` §4e already keeps `deploy_deferrals`
separate from `review_interrupts`, and it sidesteps the standing hazard that a dimension added
on only one side silently unmatches (monitoring_s4b.tf). Dimensionless on both sides therefore
holds trivially.

1. `infra/scripts/observability.sh` §4e — add two offset files
   (`INTERRUPT_BOUND_OFFSET_FILE`, `INTERRUPT_SIGNAL_OFFSET_FILE`) and two extra calls to the
   EXISTING `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` helper, whose first argument is already an ERE
   passed to `grep -cE`. The markers are JSON (`AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT {"ts": …, "reason":
   "bound-exceeded", …}`), so the patterns are the token plus the quoted reason field. Emits:
   - `review_interrupts_bound_exceeded`
   - `review_interrupts_signal_unavailable`
   - `review_interrupts` (UNCHANGED rolled-up total — existing history stays readable and a
     future third reason is still counted somewhere).
   The helper's offset/publish/clamp logic is NOT touched (bug 2dc7 owns that seam).
2. `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf` — replace the single `review_interrupts` alarm
   with two reason-scoped alarms (`rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-bound-exceeded`,
   `…-signal-unavailable`), each on its own metric, each keeping today's
   900s/1-datapoint/`Sum > 0`/`notBreaching` cadence, so aggregate sensitivity is preserved and
   `signal-unavailable` still latches on a single datapoint. Each alarm description carries only
   ITS OWN remediation. The rolled-up metric keeps being published but is no longer alarmed, so
   a firing never double-pages. Re-tuning `bound-exceeded` to be less noisy is deliberately NOT
   done here — it belongs with the deferral-bound disposition.
3. New test `tests/scripts/test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py` — drives the real
   `observability.sh` with a stubbed `journalctl`/`aws` (same harness shape as
   `test_observability_offsets_6a65.py`, which is left untouched) over a mixed journal of
   bound-exceeded and signal-unavailable markers, and asserts the three published values split
   correctly and that the rolled-up total equals their sum.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py tests/scripts/test_observability_offsets_6a65.py`
  (the second proves the untouched offset behaviour did not regress).
- `terraform fmt -check` / `terraform validate` on `infra/terraform`.
- No host shell access is needed for any of the above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A future CloudWatch-only sweep can tell `bound-exceeded` from `signal-unavailable`
      WITHOUT shell access to the host: two distinctly-named metrics and two distinctly-named
      alarms exist, each with a single reason's remediation in its description.
- [ ] `signal-unavailable` remains promptly alarming (it is the "deploys are running blind"
      case): its alarm keeps `evaluation_periods = 1` / `datapoints_to_alarm = 1`.
- [ ] Metric and alarm agree on dimensions on both sides (both DIMENSIONLESS).
- [ ] A rolled-up `review_interrupts` is still published so pre-split history stays readable.
- [ ] The split is proven by an automated test that runs the real script — not by reading it.
- [ ] The Terraform change is applied, not merely merged, and that is recorded. **This AC is
      the operator's `terraform apply`; the implementing agent cannot satisfy it, so the ticket
      stays OPEN with the merged change recorded until the apply happens.**
